item.title: [UPDATED] iPhone Mirroring: Use your iPhone from your Mac
item.description:
With iPhone Mirroring, you can wirelessly interact with your iPhone and its apps and notifications from your Mac. Your iPhone stays locked, so no one else can access it or use it to see what you’re doing.

0 added · 156 removed

-- [iPhone Mirroring system requirements](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#requirements)
-
-- [Start or stop iPhone Mirroring](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#start)
-
-- [Interact with iPhone using iPhone Mirroring](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#interact)
-
-- [Move or resize the iPhone Mirroring window](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#move-or-resize)
-
-- [Manage iPhone notifications](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#notifications)
-
-- [Copy items between devices](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#copy)
-
-- [Change iPhone Mirroring settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#settings)
-
-- [If you need help](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#help)
-
-## iPhone Mirroring system requirements
-
-iPhone Mirroring can be used with only one Mac and one iPhone at a time. Your devices must meet these requirements:
-
-- Your Mac is using macOS Sequoia 15 or later and is a [Mac with Apple silicon](https://support.apple.com/en-us/116943) or [Mac with the Apple T2 Security Chip](https://support.apple.com/en-us/103265) . Live Activities on Mac requires macOS Tahoe 26 or later.
-
-- Your iPhone is using iOS 18 or later and is [set up to use a passcode](https://support.apple.com/en-us/119586) .
-
-- Your iPhone and Mac are [signed in to the same Apple Account](https://support.apple.com/en-us/111001) using [two-factor authentication](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102660) .
-
-- Your iPhone and Mac have Bluetooth and Wi-Fi turned on.
-
-- Your iPhone is locked and near your Mac. It can also be charging and [using StandBy](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/iph878d77632/ios) .
-
-- Your Mac is not [sharing its internet connection](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchlp1540/mac) or using [AirPlay](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/mchld7e543a0/mac) or [Sidecar](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102597) .
-
-iPhone Mirroring is currently unavailable in the European Union. To simply view but not interact with your iPhone screen or its streamed video on an AirPlay-compatible device, you can [use AirPlay](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102661) instead.
-
-## Start or stop iPhone Mirroring
-
-- On your Mac, click iPhone Mirroring in the Dock. Or open it from the Applications folder or Spotlight or Siri AI . It's included with macOS Sequoia 15 or later.
-
-- If your Mac asks you to unlock your iPhone, use your iPhone to enter your iPhone passcode.
-
-- If your Mac asks whether to allow notifications from your iPhone, click Allow or Don’t Allow. You can change this later in [Notifications settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#notifications) on your Mac.
-
-- If your Mac asks whether to require Mac login to access your iPhone, choose whether to be asked every time or to authenticate automatically. You can change this later in [iPhone Mirroring settings](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#settings) .
-
-- When iPhone Mirroring shows your iPhone screen, it’s connected to your iPhone and you can use it to interact with your iPhone. [Can’t connect to your iPhone?](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#help)
-
-- To stop mirroring your iPhone, quit the iPhone Mirroring app or unlock your iPhone.
-
-If you have more than one iPhone signed in to your Apple Account and nearby, you can [choose the iPhone that your Mac uses](https://support.apple.com/en-us/120421#choose-iphone) for mirroring and iPhone notifications.
-
-
-Privacy & Security: iPhone Mirroring automatically pauses the connection after periods of inactivity. While mirroring, your iPhone says that it's in use and identifies the Mac using it. When unlocked after mirroring, it says that it was used from a Mac and links to Settings > General > AirPlay & Continuity > iPhone Mirroring, which identifies the Mac that used your iPhone, including when and for how long.
-
-## Interact with iPhone using iPhone Mirroring
-
-Tap, swipe, and type | Use your Mac mouse or trackpad to click wherever you would tap on your iPhone. Or click and hold wherever you would touch and hold, such as to edit the Home Screen or open a quick actions menu . You can scroll or swipe with your mouse or trackpad, and use your Mac keyboard to type and use keyboard shortcuts. To swipe left or right, you can also press and hold the Shift key while scrolling. To use a wireless game controller with iPhone apps that support it, use Bluetooth to connect the controller to your iPhone instead of your Mac.
-
-Go to the Home Screen | Move the pointer to the top of the iPhone Mirroring window, then click the Home Screen button in the toolbar. Or click the bar at the bottom of the iPhone Mirroring window. Or press Command-1 on your keyboard.
-
-Open the App Switcher | Move the pointer to the top of the iPhone Mirroring window, then click the App Switcher button in the toolbar. Or press Command-2 on your keyboard.
-
-Open Spotlight | Use your mouse or trackpad to scroll or swipe up from the Home Screen. Or press Command-3 on your keyboard.
-
-Open Control Center | Press Command-4 on your keyboard. (Requires macOS 27 or later.)
-
-Play audio or video | iPhone audio plays through your Mac, and your Mac controls the volume, unless you're listening through headphones connected to your iPhone. iPhone video plays back in the iPhone Mirroring window. Streaming content providers might have playback restriction policies that affect whether their premium video content can be mirrored.
-
-Access to the iPhone camera and mic is not available in iPhone Mirroring, including for Face ID or phone calls. You can [make and receive phone calls on your Mac](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102405) instead. To make calls from your Mac while iPhone Mirroring is in use, both devices must have [Wi-Fi Calling turned on](https://support.apple.com/en-us/108066) .
-
-## Move or resize the iPhone Mirroring window
-
-To change the position of the iPhone Mirroring window, move the pointer to the top of the window, then drag the window by the toolbar that appears.
-
-To change the size of the iPhone Mirroring window:
-
-- Use the View menu in the menu bar to choose from three preset sizes: Larger, Smaller, or Actual Size. Or press Command–Plus sign (+), Command–Minus sign (–), or Command-0 to switch between sizes.
-
-- In macOS 27 or later, you can drag a corner of the iPhone Mirroring window to resize it. Some apps, such as Mail, Messages, and Calendar, are designed to show more information when you drag to make the window wider. You can then return to standard iPhone size by clicking the iPhone size button in the iPhone Mirroring toolbar, or by pressing Command-9.
-
-iPhone Mirroring automatically switches to and from landscape view as required by the app that you’re using.

item.title: [UPDATED] What to expect during account recovery
item.description:
Account recovery helps you regain access to your Apple Account when you can’t reset your password. Learn what to expect during the wait, how to check your status, and the few things to do (and not to do) while you wait. Apple Support can't shorten the wait period.

29 added · 51 removed

-# How to use account recovery when you can’t reset your Apple Account password
+# What to expect during account recovery
-If you use two-factor authentication and can’t sign in or reset your password, you can regain access after an account recovery waiting period.
+Account recovery helps you regain access to your Apple Account when you can’t reset your password. Learn what to expect during the wait, how to check your status, and the few things to do (and not to do) while you wait. Apple Support can't shorten the wait period.
-## What is account recovery?
+If you haven't started account recovery, first try to change or reset your password to regain access to your account. [Learn how...](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102656)
-The account recovery process helps you reset your password and regain access to your account. If you can’t remember your Apple Account password, make sure you’ve tried everything else before starting account recovery – for example, using a different device that’s already signed in to change your password.
+## What to expect
-For security reasons, it might take several days or longer before you can use your account again after you start account recovery. Contacting Apple Support can’t help you shorten this time. This delay is inconvenient, but it’s important so that Apple can keep your account and information safe.
+- Confirmation email — You’ll receive a confirmation email (or iMessage for accounts that use only a phone number) with the specific date and time that you can expect to regain access to your Apple Account. This email arrives within 72 hours after you start account recovery.
-## Before starting account recovery
+- Wait period — For your security, account recovery might take several days or longer. This delay is inconvenient, but it’s important so that Apple can keep your account and information safe. Contacting Apple Support can’t help shorten the wait.
-Try other methods to access your account before starting account recovery.
+- Email and text or automated call when your account is ready — When your account is ready, Apple will contact you with next steps via email and by text or an automated phone call at the phone number used to start account recovery.
-- If you haven’t already, try to [reset your password](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102656) on a trusted device.
+## What not to do during the wait
-- If you don’t know which email address or phone number you use with your Apple Account, try different email addresses or phone numbers that might be associated with your Apple Account.
+A few things will interrupt or cancel your recovery request.
-- If you don’t have a device that you can use, you can [reset your password using the Apple Support app](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102656#supportapp) on a family member’s iPhone or iPad. You can also visit an Apple Store and ask to use a device.
+- Don't contact Apple Support to try to shorten the wait. They can't shorten the wait. The waiting period is fixed.
-- If you previously set up an account recovery contact, they can also [help you reset your password](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102608) .
+- Don't submit another request . Unless you find additional recovery factors, submitting another won't speed up the process and might extend the wait.
-- If you know your password, but don’t have access to your trusted phone number for verification codes, [learn what to do](https://support.apple.com/en-us/122621#no-access) .
+## What to do with your Apple devices during the wait
-## Start account recovery
+- If you started account recovery on a device with iOS 17, iPadOS 17, or macOS 27 or later, you can continue to use the device that you used to start account recovery.
-If you’ve tried everything else, start the account recovery process.
+- If you started account recovery on the web, turn off all your Apple devices during the account recovery wait.
-### On your Apple device
+- If you have another Apple device where you’re already signed in to your Apple Account, you can change your Apple Account password on that device. Your account recovery request will be canceled and you’ll be able to access your account with the new password.
-The quickest and easiest way to start account recovery is right on your device. Once you start account recovery, don’t use your other Apple devices as that might interrupt or delay the recovery process.
+- If you can’t change your password on that device — for example, if you’ve forgotten the passcode — turn it off. Using an Apple device signed in to your account will cancel your account recovery request.
-- In Settings on an iPhone or iPad, or System Settings on a Mac, try to sign in on your device.
+## If you don't receive the confirmation email
-- If you don’t know your password, you’ll get the option to start account recovery.
+Wait the full 72 hours from when you started account recovery. Then check your spam or junk folders. If you still can’t find it, go to [iforgot.apple.com](https://iforgot.apple.com) and check whether your request is active.
-- Turn off all other devices that are currently signed in with your Apple Account until account recovery is complete. If your Apple Account is in use during your request, your account recovery will be cancelled automatically.
+- If it's active, you can find the expected time for recovery on the website. The email might have been delayed.
-- If you started your account recovery in Settings, System Settings, or the Apple Support app, you can continue to use that specific device during the account recovery period.
+- If it's not active, your request might not have been submitted successfully or it might have been canceled (for example, if you used a device where you are signed in with your Apple Account during the wait). You can submit a new request to start again.
-### On the web
+## How to check your status
-You can also start account recovery on the web. Don’t use your Apple devices after starting account recovery.
+- To check your status, review the confirmation email for your expected completion time or when more information will be available.
-- Go to [iforgot.apple.com](https://iforgot.apple.com) using your device’s browser.
+- You can also check your status on [iforgot.apple.com](https://iforgot.apple.com) . Make sure to enter the same information (including the same email address and phone number) that you used to start the request. Otherwise, you might extend the wait period.
-- Click Reset Password, then follow the onscreen steps to start account recovery.
+## When the wait is over
-- Turn off all devices that are currently signed in with your Apple Account until account recovery is complete. If possible, also turn off the device that you used to start account recovery on the web. If your Apple Account is in use during your request, your account recovery will be cancelled automatically.
+- Apple will send you an email and contact you by text or automated phone call at the phone number used to start account recovery with instructions to regain access to your account.
-## After you start account recovery
+- If you don't receive the text or call, you can go directly to apple.com/recover after the time shown in your confirmation email.
-You’ll get an email 1 with a confirmation of your request and the date and time when you can expect to regain access. This email arrives within 72 hours.
+## How to cancel
-It might be several days or more before you can reset your password. Contacting Apple Support can’t help you shorten this time.
+- If you remember your password and sign in successfully, your recovery request cancels automatically and you can use your Apple Account immediately.
-1 If you have a phone number-based Apple Account without an email associated with it, you’ll receive this as an iMessage in the Messages app.
-
-### When the waiting period is over
-
-- Apple will send you a text or automated phone call with instructions to regain access to your account.
-
-- If you don’t receive the text or call, once the period specified in the original email is over, you can still go directly to [iforgot.apple.com](https://iforgot.apple.com/) . Follow the instructions to regain access to your Apple Account.
-
-### Can the waiting period be shortened?
-
-No. Contacting Apple Support can’t help you shorten this time.
-
-### Check when your account recovery request will be complete
-
-Check the email with the date and time when you can expect to regain access. This email arrives within 72 hours.
-
-You can also see how long it will be until your account is ready for recovery, or when more information will be available. Go to [iforgot.apple.com](https://iforgot.apple.com/) and enter the same Apple Account email address or phone number that you used to initiate the request.
-
-### If you need to cancel account recovery
-
-- If you remember your information and can sign in successfully, your wait period cancels automatically and you can use your Apple Account immediately.
-
-- To cancel a recovery request that you did not make, follow the instructions in your confirmation email.
+- If you didn't request account recovery, someone may be trying to access your account. Use the cancellation link in the confirmation email immediately, then consider changing your password and reviewing your account security.

+# If you forgot your password and can’t sign in to your Apple Account
-Having trouble accessing your Apple Account? Reset your password to regain access.
+Can't sign in to your Apple Account? The easiest way to reset your password is with a trusted device and your trusted phone number.
-## Use a trusted Apple device
+## Choose "Forgot Password?" and follow the onscreen instructions
-The easiest way to reset your password is with your iPhone or other trusted Apple device — one that’s already signed in to your Apple Account, so that Apple knows that it’s yours. You also need a passcode (or password on Mac) set up on that device.
+Whether you're setting up a new device, signing in to your Apple Account in the Settings app, or making a purchase in the App Store, look for "Forgot password?" or "Forgot password or don’t have an Apple Account?"

-## Reset your Apple Account password on your iPhone, iPad, or Apple Vision Pro
+A trusted device is an iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple Vision Pro, or Mac on which you’ve already signed in to your Apple Account using two-factor authentication. It’s a device that we know is yours, so it can be used to verify your identity. [Learn more about trusted devices and trusted phone numbers](https://support.apple.com/en-us/122621) .

+- If you think you know your password but can’t remember the email address or phone number for your Apple Account: try different email addresses or phone numbers that might be associated with your account. Any email address or phone number associated with your Apple Account will work to sign in.
-- Tap Change Password.
+## Change your Apple Account password on a trusted device

-- Enter your device passcode. Then follow the onscreen instructions to change your Apple Account password.
+If you have a trusted device (one that you're signed in to already with your Apple Account), you might not need to go through account recovery. Since you're already signed in on that device, you should try to change your password to something you know.

+- [Change your password on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro](https://support.apple.com/en-us/101567#ios)
-## Reset your Apple Account password on your Mac

-- From the Apple menu , choose System Settings.
+## Ways to reset your password and regain access to your Apple Account without a trusted device
-- Click [your name], then click Sign-In & Security.
+For example, you have a new iPhone with the same phone number that you’ve set up to receive verification codes from Apple.
-- Click Change Password.
+If you don’t have a trusted device, your options to reset your Apple Account password depend on what recovery factors you have.
-[Image: Mac showing sign-in and security settings.]
+### Find your recovery factors
-- Enter the password used to unlock your Mac. Then follow the onscreen instructions to change your Apple Account password.
+If you’re not signed in to a trusted Apple device, you might still be able to reset your password — but you’ll need to verify your identity. You might be asked for recovery factors such as:
-## If you’re trying to sign in on a new Apple device
+- Your trusted phone number — This is a phone number that you’ve set up to receive two-factor authentication verification codes from Apple.
-If you’re not signed in to your Apple Account on an Apple device, you can select “Forgot password or don’t have an Apple Account?” during device setup on the Apple Account sign-in screen.
+- A code from your recovery contact — If you set up a recovery contact, reach out to make sure that your recovery contact is ready to provide the 6-digit code or to help regain access in person.
-If you skipped signing in during setup, you can reset your password in Settings:
+- Your Apple Account email address — Make sure that you can access the email address associated with your Apple Account.
-- iPhone or iPad: Open the Settings app, then tap Apple Account. Select “Sign in manually”, then tap “Forgot password?” and follow the onscreen instructions.
+- The credit card associated with your Apple Account — You might be asked to confirm the CVV of the credit card associated with your Apple Account. If the verification is declined by the card issuer, you get an alert that says the information you entered is incorrect (even if you correctly entered the CVV). If this happens, select "Don't have access to this card."
